From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: Angela Park <angela.park@heliopharma.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-10-01 11:04 PDT
Subject: Re: SIG question — clarification on hosted vs dedicated vs private (scope)

Hi Angela — thanks for the clear ask. I put together a short summary below and attached a draft SIG answer matrix you can drop into your submission. High-level points: 

- Hosted (Redwood API): fully managed inference; Redwood operates control plane, runtime, and stores telemetry/metrics associated with requests. Controls labeled "Redwood-managed" in the SIG apply here. Customers do not get host-level access.

- Dedicated (Reserved capacity): dedicated GPU pools in Redwood's infrastructure backed by a contract. Runtime and operational tooling are managed by Redwood, but data isolation is guaranteed at the tenant layer. Network ingress/egress is similar to Hosted by default; some routing/egress rules can be customized as part of the Dedicated engagement (e.g., VPC peering or dedicated interconnect). Controls are mostly "Redwood-managed" but some operational configs are customer-driven.

- Private (VPC / On-prem): control plane can be customer-hosted (private control plane) and inference runtime either runs in customer-controlled VPC or on-prem hardware. Customers are responsible for host/network hardening, KMS and key custody (unless we integrate with their KMS under a managed service add-on), and physical access controls for on-prem. In SIG answers these map to "Customer-managed" for host-level and some network controls; Redwood still provides runtime patches, CVE notices, and operational guidance per the contract.

I attached: SIG_answer_matrix_v1.xlsx (draft answers columned by deployment mode) and network_boundary_diagram_v2.png. Laura + Marissa — can you confirm the Dedicated egress note (line 12 of the matrix) — whether we should explicitly call out interconnect options?

Deliverable: I can send a one-page signed scope statement (PDF) for inclusion. Target to get you final by 2027-10-05.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Date: 2027-10-02 10:21 PDT
Subject: Re: SIG question — clarification on hosted vs dedicated vs private (scope)

Hi all — quick clarifications from infra/security side: 

- For Dedicated customers we do provide VPC peering and private interconnect options in enterprise engagements. The default Dedicated setup uses isolated tenant slices inside our managed network (no cross-tenant access). Where customers require full network separation we recommend a Private deployment.

- Network diagram note: the hosted flow shows telemetry and aggregated metrics sent to Redwood monitoring services; sensitive customer payloads are not retained beyond configured retention windows unless the customer explicitly enables retention for debugging. We should include an optional note in the SIG about retention policy and where to find audit logs (Console -> Security -> Audit Logs).

- On the matrix: changed the Dedicated row for "Network egress control" to say "Configurable (peering/interconnect available)" instead of "Same as Hosted" — attached updated diagram.

Laura Bennett
Principal Product Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Hi Angela — answers below and attached are the signed scope and a small procurement note you can forward to contracts: 

1) Dedicated KMS: We support customer-managed KMS integration for Dedicated customers via our KMS connectors (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). When configured, encryption-at-rest keys are customer-owned; Redwood does not have plaintext access to keys. We will add a one-line KMS statement to the SIG matrix.

2) Private (on-prem) quarterly patching: Yes — our Private on-prem package includes an optional quarterly maintenance engagement where Redwood engineers coordinate and, if authorized, push runtime patches and provide patch reports. This is an add-on that is contractually agreed during procurement.

Deliverables attached: signed_scope_statement.pdf (signed by Legal), updated_SIG_answer_matrix_v2.xlsx (includes KMS and patching language), procurement_note_private_quarterly_patching.pdf (short note for procurement).
